text:
Well, successfully survived my first year here at NSU. So, I will be sharing brief review about all the courses and faculties I have done this year.
Bio103- NIA- One of the best faculty I have come across at NSU. Easygoing for those who will take Bio103 as GED from non-science background or from an engineering major. He wants students to draw figures in mid and final. Counts best 2 or 3 out of 4 quiz. Questions are directly from the slides. Takes review class before exams.
Che101- ABI- You may find his classes boring, but other than that he is quite chill. The contents are very easy, like a watered down version of what you studied in HSC. Everything in the exams comes directly from the slides. Make sure that you don’t skip anything. Sometimes, he will make some unexpected questions, from slides that we may overlook thinking it’s unimportant. He graded fairly for me and for everyone I knew in my section. I know some people say that he decurves or gives unexpected grades, so be careful about that I guess. Counts 2 out of 3 quiz, and there is mid and final.
Eng103- FTN- Such a sweet faculty. She puts a lot of effort in teaching. As for grading, I felt she could have graded more leniently but maybe that was just me trying to blend in with NSU grading system. Assessments includes assignments, quizzes, mid and final.
Mat116- AdA- Honestly, not good for learning. Most of the times you won’t even get what he is saying. Great for grading though. He doesn’t lengthen the syllabus and mainly focuses on examples of each chapter. He will hand out short suggestion before mid or final, and all the questions will be from those. Quizzes are straight forward, directly from book examples.
Che101L- KFR- She is exactly how a faculty is supposed to be. Student friendly about teaching but strict about discipline. Don’t slack off in her class. Don’t be late and don’t use your phone in the class. Make sure that you wear lab coats in each class and bring a printed copy of the lab manual with you. All these may be reasons you lose marks for attendance and participation.
About lab reports, she wants them to be neat and clean and well organized. Use pencil to write lab reports. Ma’am will give instructions about how to write them, make sure you follow them. Especially for certain questions, she urges us to write the way she wants. Be careful about those.
Final question was very easy and from the basics. Make sure that you bring your own stationaries (e.g. pencils, sharpeners, calculators).
Bio103L- KMRH- Sir was so chill whole semester. We had to submit the lab reports on the final day. So, you will get a lot of time to work on them. However, make sure that you don’t miss a single class. Each attendance is worth 5 marks. If you do miss any class, contact with sir immediately. Also, the final exam is 50 marks but the lecture slide’s contents are very little. So, when you take prep for the final exam, don’t skip anything.
His103- SdH1- In his class, you will feel like you’re listening to one long story in installment. Never in my life had I thought History classes can be so interesting. He is super humble and such a great person. Quiz questions are directly from lecture slides, which are somewhat detailed. Mid & Final involves board questions. Even though they’re directly from the slide, for some questions sir expects very specific answers. If you are able to write that specific answer, you will get full marks, otherwise he will deduct some marks. Therefore, you have to be very attentive in the class, because he will literally mention in between lectures whether there will be any question from a specific topic or not, and tell you answers for those specific questions as well.
There was project where we had to make a poster about a martyred intellectual, and give a presentation on it. Sir was super easy going about that, like almost everyone scored 19/20 or 20/20. Just try to make the poster look eye catching, dress up formally, and try to speak in front of the class.
Sir also curves everyone by one grade.
Counts best 2 out of 3 quizzes. Other assessments include mid, project, presentation and final.
Sadly, he is not with NSU anymore. Summer 25 was his last semester.
Bio201, Che202, BBT221, Che202L- TSHq- Ma’am is one of the sweetest faculties I have ever met. She teaches so enthusiastically, asks whether we have questions after finishing each segment, is very responsive in email and you can visit her in her office period to clear confusions. If you want to learn, you will end the semester with great experience. She is someone who is truly enjoying what she is doing.
Now let’s talk about her question pattern, which is probably most talked about. Her questions are conceptual, very conceptual. If you want questions directly from lecture slides or if you think you will be able to answer with half-baked understanding of the topics, you will be disappointed. That’s not all. If you plan to study on the night before exam, you will face trouble too. You have to be consistent, study regularly, have crystal clear concept of the topics, practice the sample questions she will give and overall put a lot of effort.
She will give bonus marks in quizzes (2 marks), mid and final (3 marks). She also takes bonus assignment worth 5 marks. She even gave us bonus marks for attending make up classes, and said in the first class she will curve 1-1.5 marks. Also takes bonus assignments worth 5 marks.
Counts best 3 out of 5 quizzes. Other assessments include mid and final.
As for the lab reports, she wants them to be very precise, and unlike other faculties posts some questions for the ‘discussion’ section of the lab report and you gotta answer each of them. She will go sentence by sentence in the lab reports, so, you gotta be very careful about it. Apart from lab report, there is only final exam and that contains bonus questions as well.
Che201- SNht- I know there are a lot of positive reviews about ma’am on the groups, but there are some things that you need to know. First, around 80% topics of this course are from HSC. I didn’t have any trouble understanding them. However, for topics that were not in HSC like Chemical Kinetics or Photochemistry, I had quite trouble in the class understanding ma’am’s lectures. Basically, I had to depend on self-study for those.
Quiz, mid and final questions are fairly easy and from the slides. Sometimes, even the maths were directly from the slides. For some questions, she wants us to answer them in a specific way, and she will give guideline about that in the class. That’s something you have to keep in mind. Also, I’m not sure but she may have curved 1 mark.
Counts best 3 out of 5 quizzes. Other assessments include mid and final.
Che203- MAR5- In simple words, just brilliant. Every time I attended his class I felt so motivated and felt like knowing and learning as much as one can. The course itself is quite hard. It’s full of long ass mechanisms, structures, and other complex chemistries and even the theoretical questions are conceptual. If you take this course under him, remember two things. One, time management can be a huge issue in quizzes, so be prepared for that mentally. Two, be attentive in his class, not everything he mentions during lectures is on the slides. Take notes or photos as necessary. Counts 3/4 quiz. Other assessments are mid and final. Questions in mid or final are relatively straight forward. He doesn’t curve though and gives you exactly what you deserve.
Bio201L- SMDA- He takes quizzes right after lab for experiment 1-3 . All the lecture modules are posted on canvas beforehand. So, you can take preparations in advance. For experiment 4 & 5, you have to write the lab report again right after lab, which isn’t that big of a deal tbh. Make sure you do the calculations right and draw the graphs correctly. He gave everyone full marks for both lab reports in our section. Final exam felt a little tricky; DO NOT skip anything from the lecture modules. Each of them is like 3-4 pages.
Bio202- FHo- Another chill faculty. Teaches well, doesn’t give a huge syllabus, and marks graciously. Takes review classes before mid and final and mentions all the important topics there. So, as long as you learn them, you can do well in both exams. Counts 3/4 quiz and quiz questions are very easy. Takes a viva which usually includes the final exam syllabus. If you prepare for viva, final preparations are like 90% done there.
Bus172- MKz- He teaches really well. Questions are straight forward and from the slides. Counts 1/2 quiz. There is two mid and the final exam. He curves by one grade until B+. So, if you get B+ he will give A-. However won’t curve if you get A- Now, here is the tricky part. There is like lot of questions in the exam compared to the time given. That goes for both mids, final and quizzes. Finishing your paper before time runs out can be a hassle.
Eco101- AYO- Tbh, I had a lot of troubles understanding his lectures and that goes for most of the students in the section. He teaches fast and its like expects students to know things beforehand. I really struggled in mid-1. The course itself isn’t that hard considering his syllabus is very small. So, got the hang of it by mid-2 and final. I also think he curved but I can’t be entirely sure. So, I would say don’t take him unless you have knowledge of economics from HSC or A level, or if you’re confident about self-studying.

MHSn for MAT116 is extremely good. She does not decurve.
